title: Switching-lemma bound on decision-tree depth after a random restriction
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function on $n\ge 1$ variables, and let $d,s,w,l,t$ be natural numbers with $d\ge 2$ and $s,w,l\ge 1$. Suppose $f$ is computed by some Boolean circuit of depth at most $d$, size at most $s$, and fan-in at most $w$. Draw a random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables in which each variable is independently left free with probability
\[
  p \;=\; \frac{1}{40w}\left(\frac{1}{40l}\right)^{d-2},
\]
and is otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $(1-p)/2$; let $f\restriction_\rho$ denote the function of the free variables obtained by substituting the fixed values into $f$. Then the probability that $f\restriction_\rho$ cannot be computed by any decision tree of depth at most $t$ satisfies
\[
  \bbP\!\left[\,\text{decision-tree depth of } f\restriction_\rho > t\,\right]
  \;\le\; s\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t}
  + s\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120w}\right) + s\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{n}{120l}\right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
f is computed by a circuit of depth <= d, size <= s, fan-in <= w
restriction is Bernoulli with parameter composedDelta(w,l,d)
